description.narrative:
African Biodiversity Network (ABN), det Afrikanska nätverket för biologiskt mångfald, har till Sida ansökt om finansiering för genomförande av "Bevarande av biokulturell mångfald genom att stärka motståndskraften i samhällen och ekosystemen" till ett belopp av 14 450 000 SEK för perioden 2021-2024. Den föreslagna insatsens övergripande mål är att bygga upp och stärka bevarandet av biokulturell mångfalds praxis och livsmedels suveränintet i Afrika, genom kapacitetsuppbyggnad, nätverkande och försvar av densamma. Föreslagen insats ska adressera bevarande av biologisk mångfald och koppla samman denna med kulturella perspektiv vilka bidrar till ett brett mål för att stärka och diversifiera lokalsamhällenas inkomstmöjligheter.
Insatsen bygger på ABN´s existerande grundläggande arbete och fokuserar på fyra sammanlänkade program nämligen: 1) Lokalsamhällenas ekologiska styrning (Community Ecological Governance CEG)- En naturcentrerad process som ska återuppliva traditionell kunskap, praxis och styrningssystem för att återuppbygga samhällen 2) Försörjnings- och ekosystem kunskap i samhällena om fröer och sorter i samarbete med kvinnor, män och äldre för att återuppliva lokal traditionell frökunskap och liknande kunskap för att stärka frö och mat suveräniteten och återvinna den biologiska mångfalden. 3) Ungdomskultur och biologisk mångfald- sätta unga människor i kontakt med natur, kultur och sin roll i sammanhanget, 4) Stärkt nätverksbyggande, kommunikation och förespråkande av kulturell biologisk mångfald- nätverka med likasinnade på individ- och organisationsnivå för att katalysera större aktivitet och influera policies och allmänhetens uppfattning inom ekologi och socioekonomi som påverkar Afrika. De fyra tematiska områdena fokuserar i princip på att bemyndiga ursprungsbefolkningar och lokalsamhällen att återuppliva sin biokulturella mångfald och skydda områden av ekologisk, spirituell, social och ekonomisk betydelse. ABN ska genomföra insatsen tillsammans med genomförande partners i 20 afrikanska länder.
Totalkostnaden för ABN´s föreslagna insats är nära 42 miljoner svenska kronor vilket indikeras i den bifogade budgetplanen (bilaga 2). ABN efterfrågar Sida´s finansiering för 34 procent av den totalakostnaden. ABN har säkrat en tilläggsfinansiering på 38 procent på 16 miljoner svenska kronor från Bread for the World och Swedbio och arbetar för att säkra finansiering av den utstående balansen av projektkostnaden. För detta ändamål beviljar Sida medel till en summa av 14 450 000 svenska kronor vilket bidrar till ABNs övergripande arbete vilken synliggörs i organisationens konsoliderade budgetplan.

That Sida shall contribute to " Conserving Bio-cultural Diversity through Strengthening Community and Ecosystem Resilience" 2021 - 2024, with 3 050 000 kronor 2021; 4 800 000 kronor 2022; 4 800 000 kronor 2023; and 1 800 000 kroner 2024.
That 3 050 000 kronor shall be allocated for this purpose from the financial code 106160300 in 2021.
That 11 400 000 kronor for this purpose shall be allocated from the framework for outstanding commitments with the indicative distribution at Sida's budget (per year) above.
That the Head of Regional Development Cooperation in Sub-Saharan Africa on behalf of Sida shall sign the agreement with African Biodiversity Network (ABN) principally in accordance with the enclosed draft agreement.

PROJECT GOAL: To contribute to improved life on land through conservation of bio-cultural diversity, restoration of terrestrial and marine ecosystems in Africa. PROJECT OBJECTIVES OVER THE THREE YEARS PERIOD: 1) Strengthened and diversified community livelihood options based on good bio-cultural diversity and seed governance. 2) Community ecological governance system revived, based on time-tested community knowledge and practices. 3) Proactive youth movement established that celebrates and engages with issues on biocultural diversity across Africa. 4) Increased support for community-led advocacy as a prerequisite for building coalitions for policy influence on prioritized issues. 5) Improved networking and practice of methodologies among communities, partners and allies within the network

description.narrative:
Summary of Acheivements by Outcome
Outcome 1: Seed and Bio-cultural Diversity Revived at Community Level
The contribution has significantly strengthened seed sovereignty and revived indigenous seed systems. Over 150 varieties of indigenous seeds were identified, recuperated, and preserved through community-driven initiatives. Six partners developed seed catalogues where documented some of these seeds (ABN Partners' Seed Catalogues - Google Drive). Farmers established 16 Community Learning Centers (CLCs) across Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Gabon, Morocco, and Zimbabwe, serving as hubs for training and seed conservation. Over 9,000 households, many led by women, participated in agroecological farming practices, leading to enhanced food sovereignty and resilience against climate change. These achievements directly contributed to the conservation of bio-cultural diversity and restoration of terrestrial ecosystems by enhancing indigenous seed systems, strengthening food sovereignty, and preserving traditional knowledge critical to ecosystem health and resilience.
Outcome 2: Strengthened Community Ecological Governance
The project empowered 95 communities across 14 countries to revive and strengthen traditional ecological governance. Through community dialogues, ecological mapping, and participatory resource management, communities reclaimed stewardship over Sacred Natural Sites (SNS) and territories. The project supported the Buliisa district communities to draft ordinances protecting SNS, while in Egypt, the renewal of the Lake Nasser bird hunting ban was celebrated as a major conservation victory. In Kenya, Zimbabwe, and Cameroon, traditional leadership structures were revitalized, with elders guiding sustainable land and watershed management practices. More than 50 community-driven ecological maps were created, showcasing past, present, and future visions of landscapes, enhancing ownership and advocacy power at local and national levels.
Outcome 3: Youth Movement Established and Strengthened
Throughout the three years, the project intentionally invested in building a strong, proactive youth movement committed to agroecology, conservation, and the revitalization of bio-cultural diversity. Over 4,000 youth actively engaged through various initiatives, including agroecology training, seed saving campaigns, tree planting activities, and nature excursions. Youth-led projects such as watershed management initiatives in Zimbabwe, establishment of agroecology demonstration farms in Tanzania, and seed preservation campaigns in Rwanda and Kenya demonstrated the growing agency of young leaders. A major milestone was achieved during the 2024 AgroBioCulture (ABC) Festival in Togo, which convened youth representatives from across Africa. A key highlight of the festival was the launch of the "Youth Voices in Biodiversity and Agroecology in Africa" reportcommissioned by ABN as a region-wide study on youth perspectives, challenges, and aspirations in biodiversity governance and agroecological transformation. The report amplified the voices of young people and emphasized their crucial role in shaping the future of agroecological and cultural resilience across the continent. Empowering youth to lead in agroecological transformation and biodiversity conservation nurtures a new generation of custodians who will sustain and advance efforts to restore terrestrial and marine ecosystems, ensuring long-term resilience and continuity of indigenous knowledge systems critical for life on land.
Outcome 4: Enhanced Community-led Advocacy and Policy Influence
Advocacy was a cornerstone of the project, recognizing ABN's nature as a network deeply rooted in movement building. Over the three years, ABN and its partners implemented a range of strategic advocacy actions that significantly influenced biodiversity, food sovereignty, and community rights discourses both nationally and regionally. More than 40 advocacy campaigns and high-level engagements were initiated, covering issues such as protection of indigenous seeds, farmers' rights, land tenure, safeguarding Sacred Natural Sites (SNS), and climate justice. ABN partners were instrumental in lobbying during national dialogues on agroecology policies, biodiversity frameworks, and seed sovereignty legislations in countries like Uganda, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Benin, and Ethiopia. Through targeted engagements, ABN helped influence policy spaces at events like the Africa Climate Week, CBD COP forums, and local government processes. ABN also built strategic alliances with research institutions, policy advocacy groups, and farmer organizations, catalyzing coalitions that continue to drive systemic change in favor of agroecology and bio-cultural diversity conservation. By spearheading community-led advocacy and influencing policy processes, the project created enabling environments critical for the conservation of bio-cultural diversity, securing of farmers and indigenous peoples rights, and restoration of resilient terrestrial and marine ecosystems.
Outcome 5: Strengthened ABN Networking and Practice of Methodologies
The strengthening of ABNs network and methodologies was fundamental to ensuring sustainability, cross-regional collaboration, and scaling impact. Throughout the three years, ABN successfully revitalized its Sub-Regional Nodes (SRNs) East Africa, West Africa, Southern Africa, and North/Central Africa SRNs has been established as key coordination and learning platforms. Through SRN meetings, joint strategy sessions, thematic learning exchanges, and partner-led workshops, ABN fostered greater horizontal peer-to-peer learning across different countries. These platforms also allowed for collective planning, ensuring that activities at the country level aligned with the broader ABN strategic vision and thematic priorities. Strengthening coordination, collaboration, and the operational effectiveness of the ABN network fostered a stronger, unified voice for bio-cultural diversity and agroecology advocacy, amplified grassroots impacts, and ensured sustained action toward conserving ecosystems and enhancing life on land and in associated marine areas.
